records.source: לְֽ֭תַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ נִפְרָ֑ד בְּכָל־תּ֝וּשִׁיָּ֗ה יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃
records.gloss: For desire seeks [one] separating himself; against all sound wisdom he breaks out.
pieces: Whoever keeps apart from others pursues selfish desires \q and lashes out at all good sense.

L.1: One who separates {{gender:themselves|himself}} seeks [their own] desire; \q {{gender:they break|he breaks}} out against all sound wisdom.

R.1: People who stay away from others only care about what they want. \q They argue against good advice.

decisions.choice: one who separates himself: the unfriendly loner, or the divisive
alternatives: one who breaks with others seeks a pretext
decisions.reason: The line is hard. With a small change "desire" reads "pretext": the divisive person looks for an excuse to quarrel.

decisions.choice: breaks out: bursts into a quarrel
decisions.reason: The verb of 17:14 and 20:3.

records.source: לֹֽא־יַחְפֹּ֣ץ כְּ֭סִיל בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה כִּ֝֗י אִֽם־בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת לִבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in revealing his heart.
pieces: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, \q only in airing his own opinions.

L.2: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, \q but only in airing {{gender:their|his}} own opinions.

R.2: Fools do not want to understand. \q They only want to tell everyone what they think.

decisions.choice: revealing his heart: showing what he thinks
decisions.reason: The heart is the mind (2:2).

records.source: בְּֽבוֹא־רָ֭שָׁע בָּ֣א גַם־בּ֑וּז וְֽעִם־קָל֥וֹן חֶרְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: When a wicked [person] comes, contempt also comes, and with dishonor, reproach.
pieces: With wickedness comes contempt, \q and with shame comes disgrace.

L.3: When [the] wicked comes, contempt also comes, \q and with dishonor [comes] disgrace.

R.3: When people do evil, others look down on them. \q When they do shameful things, they are disgraced.

decisions.choice: the wicked: or wickedness
decisions.reason: With other vowels "the wicked" reads "wickedness", which matches the second line.

records.source: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים דִּבְרֵ֣י פִי־אִ֑ישׁ נַ֥חַל נֹ֝בֵ֗עַ מְק֣וֹר חָכְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Deep waters [are the] words of [the] mouth of a person; a flowing stream, a fountain of wisdom.
pieces: A person's words can be deep waters, \q and the spring of wisdom a rushing stream.

L.4: [The] words of a person's mouth [are] deep waters; \q [the] fountain of wisdom [is] a flowing stream.

R.4: What people say can be hard to understand, like deep water. \q But wisdom is like a clear, fresh stream.

decisions.choice: deep waters ... a flowing stream: contrast or parallel
decisions.reason: The lines may be parallel (wise words are deep and fresh) or set in contrast (words can be murky, but wisdom flows clear; compare 20:5).

records.source: שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא־ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: To lift up [the] face of a wicked [person] [is] not good, to turn aside a righteous [person] in judgment.
pieces: It is not good to favor the guilty \q or to deny justice to the innocent.

L.5: To show favor to [the] wicked [is] not good, \q [nor] to deprive [the] righteous of justice.

R.5: It is wrong for a judge to favor the guilty. \q It is wrong to be unfair to innocent people.

decisions.choice: lift up the face: show partiality
decisions.reason: A legal idiom for taking sides unfairly (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 1:17).

records.source: שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃
records.gloss: [The] lips of a fool go into strife, and his mouth calls for blows.
pieces: A fool's lips lead him into quarrels, \q and his mouth asks for a beating.

L.6: A fool's lips walk into strife, \q and {{gender:their|his}} mouth invites a beating.

R.6: Fools get into arguments because of what they say. \q Their words can get them beaten.

decisions.choice: a beating: blows
decisions.reason: The word (mahalumot) is blows (19:29).

records.source: פִּֽי־כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה־ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] mouth of a fool [is] ruin to him, and his lips [are] a snare of his life.
pieces: A fool's mouth is his undoing, \q and his lips trap his own life.

L.7: A fool's mouth [is] {{gender:their|his}} ruin, \q and {{gender:their|his}} lips [are] a snare for {{gender:their|his}} life.

R.7: Foolish people ruin themselves by what they say. \q Their own words trap them.

decisions.choice: a snare: as in 12:13

records.source: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
records.gloss: [The] words of a slanderer [are] like delicacies, and they go down [into the] chambers of [the] belly.
pieces: Gossip is like tasty bites of food; \q it goes all the way down inside.

L.8: [The] words of a gossip [are] like tasty morsels; \q they go down into [the] inner rooms of [the] belly.

R.8: People love to hear gossip, the way they love tasty food. \q And it stays with them.

decisions.choice: tasty morsels: delicacies, gulped down
decisions.reason: The word (mitlahamim) is rare, most likely "things swallowed greedily". The saying returns in 26:22.

records.source: גַּ֭ם מִתְרַפֶּ֣ה בִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא לְבַ֣עַל מַשְׁחִֽית׃
records.gloss: Also [one] slack in his work, he [is] a brother to a master of destruction.
pieces: Anyone who is slack in their work \q is close kin to someone who destroys.

L.9: Whoever is slack in {{gender:their|his}} work \q [is] also a brother to one who destroys.

R.9: A lazy worker is almost as bad as someone who destroys things.

decisions.choice: brother to a destroyer: as bad as a vandal
decisions.reason: Neglect does damage as surely as destruction does.

records.source: מִגְדַּל־עֹ֭ז שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בּֽוֹ־יָר֖וּץ צַדִּ֣יק וְנִשְׂגָּֽב׃
records.gloss: A tower of strength [is the] name of YHWH; into it [the] righteous runs and is set on high.
pieces: The name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a fortress tower; \q the righteous run to it and are kept safe on high.

L.10: [The] name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a strong tower; \q [the] righteous runs into it and is safe.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is like a strong tower. \q Good people can run to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and be safe.

decisions.choice: the name of the LORD: the LORD himself, as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: The name stands for God's person and character (Psalm 20:2; Exodus 34:5–7).

decisions.choice: is safe: is set on high, out of reach
decisions.reason: The verb (sagab) means to be lifted out of danger (29:25; Psalm 91:14).

records.source: ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ וּכְחוֹמָ֥ה נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] wealth of a rich [person] [is] his strong city, and like a high wall in his imagination.
pieces: The rich think their wealth is a fortified city, \q a high wall around them, but only in their imagination.

L.11: [The] wealth of [the] rich [is] {{gender:their|his}} strong city, \q and like a high wall in {{gender:their|his}} imagination.

R.11: Rich people think their money will protect them like a strong wall. \q But they are only imagining it.

decisions.choice: a strong city: as in 10:15, now set beside verse 10
decisions.reason: Verse 10 names the true strong tower; the rich man's wall is "in his imagination".

records.source: לִפְנֵי־שֶׁ֭בֶר יִגְבַּ֣הּ לֵב־אִ֑ישׁ וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Before destruction the heart of a person is haughty, and before honor [is] humility.
pieces: A proud heart goes before a fall, \q and humility comes before honor.

L.12: Before destruction a person's heart is proud, \q but humility [comes] before honor.

R.12: Pride comes before ruin. \q Humility comes before honor.

records.source: מֵשִׁ֣יב דָּ֭בָר בְּטֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִוֶּ֥לֶת הִיא־ל֝֗וֹ וּכְלִמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: [One] returning a word before he hears, it [is] folly to him and shame.
pieces: To answer before listening \q is foolish and shameful.

L.13: Whoever answers before {{gender:they listen|he listens}}, \q it [is] folly and shame to {{gender:them|him}}.

R.13: It is foolish and embarrassing to answer before you have heard the whole question.

decisions.choice: answers before listening
decisions.reason: Compare verse 17 and James 1:19.

records.source: רֽוּחַ־אִ֭ישׁ יְכַלְכֵּ֣ל מַחֲלֵ֑הוּ וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה מִ֣י יִשָּׂאֶֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: [The] spirit of a person will endure his sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear it?
pieces: The human spirit can hold up under illness, \q but who can bear a broken spirit?

L.14: A person's spirit can endure {{gender:their|his}} sickness, \q but a crushed spirit, who can bear [it]?

R.14: A strong spirit can help you get through sickness. \q But if your spirit is broken, it is very hard to keep going.

decisions.choice: spirit: inner strength, courage

records.source: לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יִקְנֶה־דָּ֑עַת וְאֹ֥זֶן חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תְּבַקֶּשׁ־דָּֽעַת׃
records.gloss: A discerning heart acquires knowledge, and [the] ear of wise [people] seeks knowledge.
pieces: A discerning mind gains knowledge, \q and the wise listen out for more.

L.15: [The] heart of [the] discerning acquires knowledge, \q and [the] ear of [the] wise seeks knowledge.

R.15: People who understand keep learning. \q Wise people listen so they can learn more.

decisions.choice: acquires ... seeks: the wise keep learning (1:5)
decisions.reason: See 1:5 and 9:9.

records.source: מַתָּ֣ן אָ֭דָם יַרְחִ֣יב ל֑וֹ וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְדֹלִ֣ים יַנְחֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] gift of a person makes room for him, and before great [people] it leads him.
pieces: A gift opens doors for the giver \q and brings him into the presence of the great.

L.16: A person's gift makes room for {{gender:them|him}}, \q and brings {{gender:them|him}} before [the] great.

R.16: A gift can open doors for you \q and help you meet important people.

decisions.choice: gift: a present, not necessarily a bribe
decisions.reason: The word (mattan) is a present (Genesis 32:13). The saying observes how gifts work; compare 17:8 and 21:14.

records.source: צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ וּבָֽא־רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Righteous [is] the first in his case, and his neighbor comes and examines him.
pieces: The first to state a case sounds right, \q until the other side comes and asks questions.

L.17: The first to plead {{gender:their|his}} case [seems] right, \q until {{gender:their|his}} neighbor comes and cross-examines {{gender:them|him}}.

R.17: In an argument, the first person to speak seems to be right. \q But then someone else asks questions and shows the other side.

decisions.choice: and comes, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) lack the "and"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: case ... cross-examines: in court
decisions.reason: Hearing both sides is basic to justice (Deuteronomy 1:16).

records.source: מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: The lot puts an end to contentions and between mighty [people] separates.
pieces: Casting lots settles disputes \q and keeps powerful opponents apart.

L.18: The lot ends quarrels \q and settles [matters] between [the] powerful.

R.18: Throwing lots can settle an argument between powerful people.

decisions.choice: the lot: as in 16:33

records.source: אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת־עֹ֑ז וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: A brother offended [is] more than a strong city, and contentions [are] like [the] bar of a fortress.
pieces: A brother wronged is harder to win back than a fortified city; \q quarrels are like the bolted gates of a castle.

L.19: An offended brother [is harder to win] than a strong city, \q and quarrels [are] like [the] bars of a fortress.

R.19: It is harder to make peace with a brother you have hurt than to capture a city. \q Family fights can shut people out like locked gates.

decisions.choice: contentions, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The ketiv and qere give two spellings of "contentions"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: an offended brother: hard to win back
alternatives: a brother helped is a strong city (the ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is terse. The ancient Greek reads it positively: a brother helped by a brother is like a strong city.

records.source: מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע׃
records.gloss: From [the] fruit of [the] mouth of a person his belly is satisfied; [with the] produce of his lips he is satisfied.
pieces: People will be filled by the fruit of their words; \q they will be satisfied by the harvest of their lips.

L.20: A person's belly is filled from [the] fruit of {{gender:their|his}} mouth; \q {{gender:they are|he is}} filled [with the] harvest of {{gender:their|his}} lips.

R.20: What you say will come back to you, \q like a harvest you have to eat.

decisions.choice: the fruit of the mouth: as in 12:14 and 13:2

records.source: מָ֣וֶת וְ֭חַיִּים בְּיַד־לָשׁ֑וֹן וְ֝אֹהֲבֶ֗יהָ יֹאכַ֥ל פִּרְיָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Death and life [are] in [the] hand of [the] tongue, and those loving it will eat its fruit.
pieces: The tongue has the power of life and death, \q and those who love to talk will eat what it produces.

L.21: Death and life [are] in [the] power of [the] tongue, \q and those who love it will eat its fruit.

R.21: Words can bring life or death. \q People who talk a lot will have to live with what they say.

decisions.choice: those who love it: those who love to talk, or love the tongue's power
decisions.reason: Whoever loves using the tongue will eat its fruit, good or bad.

records.source: מָצָ֣א אִ֭שָּׁה מָ֣צָא ט֑וֹב וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: [He who] finds a wife finds good and obtains favor from YHWH.
pieces: The man who finds a wife finds something good \q and receives favor from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.22: [He who] finds a wife finds good \q and obtains favor from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.22: A man who finds a wife has found something good. \q It shows that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is kind to him.

decisions.choice: finds a wife ... finds good: as with Wisdom
decisions.reason: Compare 8:35: "whoever finds me finds life and obtains favor from the LORD." A good wife is a gift of God (19:14; 31:10). The ancient Greek adds "a good wife".

records.source: תַּחֲנוּנִ֥ים יְדַבֶּר־רָ֑שׁ וְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר יַעֲנֶ֥ה עַזּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Supplications [the] poor speaks, but [the] rich answers harshly.
pieces: The poor must beg for mercy; \q the rich can afford to answer roughly.

L.23: [The] poor speaks pleadings, \q but [the] rich answers harshly.

R.23: Poor people have to beg politely. \q Rich people can answer rudely.

decisions.choice: an observation of how things are
decisions.reason: Compare 14:20 and 19:7.

records.source: אִ֣ישׁ רֵ֭עִים לְהִתְרֹעֵ֑עַ וְיֵ֥שׁ אֹ֝הֵ֗ב דָּבֵ֥ק מֵאָֽח׃
records.gloss: A man of companions [is] to be broken, but there is a friend clinging more than a brother.
pieces: Someone with many companions may still be ruined, \q but some friends stay closer than a brother.

L.24: A person of many companions may come to ruin, \q but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

R.24: Having lots of friends will not always help you. \q But some friends are more loyal than family.

decisions.choice: come to ruin: be broken, or be friendly
alternatives: has friends just to be sociable
decisions.reason: The verb (hitroea) may mean "be ruined" or (from another root) "be friendly". The contrast is between many casual friends and one loyal one.

decisions.choice: sticks: clings
decisions.reason: The verb (dabaq) of Genesis 2:24 and Ruth 1:14.
